classification.difficultyReason: Explain that the labelled lengths are a side and perpendicular height rather than diagonals, using equal sides to identify a suitable base and justify the correct formula.

inlines.text: Explain why the area of this rhombus is NOT

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2 figure at the lower left
spec.description: Unshaded right-slanting rhombus with horizontal top and bottom sides, matching double equality ticks on all four sides, a side labelled 10 cm, and a red dashed vertical height labelled 8 cm with a right-angle marker at its foot.
spec.mathematics: All four sides are equal. The perpendicular height is 8 cm and a side is 10 cm; these measurements are not the diagonals.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied measurements and marks remain visible in the question. The explanation and calculated area appear only in answer fields.

answer.short: The $8\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$ measurements are the perpendicular height and a side, not the diagonals. Treat the rhombus as a parallelogram and use $A=bh$.
answer.worked:
The formula $A=\dfrac{xy}{2}$ requires the lengths of the diagonals. Here, $8\text{ cm}$ is the perpendicular height and $10\text{ cm}$ is a side. All four sides are equal, so the base is also $10\text{ cm}$. Use the parallelogram formula:
$$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\A&=10\times8\\A&=80\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
